title: Check if Array Is Good
hints: with n = array length - 1, a good array's sorted form is 1, 2, 3, ..., n-1, n, n. notice every value except n has a single unique home index, and n has to share the last index with itself
values 1 through n-1 belong at index value-1, exactly like in a standard cyclic sort. both copies of n want index n-1, the last slot in a zero-indexed array of length n+1

run cyclic placement: for each position, while the value there isn't already correct and its target slot doesn't already hold the right value, swap it toward home, treating any value equal to n as wanting the last index
after placement, check every index i from 0 to n-2 holds i+1, and the last index holds n. if anything mismatches, or if a value outside [1, n] ever appears, the array isn't good
commonMistakes: computing n as the array length instead of array length minus one
not handling the case where both copies of n want the same last index, which needs a special-cased placement rule instead of the usual value-1 index formula
not rejecting values greater than n or less than 1, which can never belong in a good array

content.problemStatement:
Let `n` be one less than the length of the input array. An array is considered "good" if, once sorted ascending, it looks exactly like 1, 2, 3, ..., n-1, n, n: a permutation of every integer from 1 to n, where n itself appears twice instead of once (the two copies of n can sit anywhere before sorting).

**Given an array, determine whether it is good.**
notes: the value n appears twice but one of 1..n-1 is missing or duplicated instead
the array contains a value greater than n, which can never be part of a good array

optimal.pattern: cyclic sort placement: with n = array length - 1, values 1..n-1 each belong at index value-1, and both copies of n compete for the last index; place everything and check the final layout matches the target

bruteForce.approach: count the frequency of every value with a hash map, then check that values 1..n-1 each appear exactly once, n appears exactly twice, and no value outside that range is present
